findings.finding: For 2^m runners, any permutation of final scores (0…2^m‑1) can be realized by suitable pairings and speed order; thus N=(2^20)!. k=v₅((2^20)!)=⌊2^20/5⌋+⌊2^20/25⌋+…=262140. Answer=262140 mod 10⁵=62140.

Key: Final scores are unique binary numbers (0‑2²⁰‑1). Ranking = leaf order of a binary tree where each node splits its set into equal halves (winners/losers) via a matching where each winner is faster than its opponent. A split of a set of size 2ⁿ is possible iff the winner set satisfies “in any prefix of fastest k, winners ≤⌊k/2⌋”, i.e. Catalan number C_{2^{n‑1}} choices. Recursively, total orderings  

N = ∏_{j=0}^{19} (C_{2^{j}})^{2^{19‑j}}, C_n = (1/(n+1))·(2n choose n).  

Exponent of prime p in N: S_p = Σ_{j=0}^{19} 2^{19‑j}[v_p((2^{j+1})!) – 2v_p((2^{j})!) – v_p(2^{j}+1)].  

Compute: S₂=524 287, S₅=121 818 → k = min = 121 818.  

Answer = 121 818 mod 10⁵ = **21 818**.

Tree of depth 20; each node’s left/right leaves must interleave as a Dyck word → f(d)=Catalan(2^{d‑1})·f(d‑1)^2.  
N=∏_{j=0}^{19}C_{2^j}^{2^{19‑j}}.  
v₂(N)=524 287, v₅(N)=121 818 ⇒ k=min=121 818.  
k mod 10⁵=21 818.
N = ∏_{i=1}^{20}((2^i−1)!! )^{2^{20−i}}; each (2^i−1)!! is odd ⇒ v₂(N)=0. Hence 10^k∣N ⇒ k=min(v₂,v₅)=0. Answer: 0. (Check no ties: each leaf gets 1 runner.)

Final scores are distinct binary numbers (0‑2²⁰‑1). Rankings ↔ leaf order of a full binary tree. At each node of size 2ⁿ, winner set must satisfy w_i>l_i ⇒ Catalan C_{2^{n‑1}} choices.  

Recurrence: f(0)=1, f(d)=C_{2^{d‑1}}·f(d‑1)².  

Thus N=∏_{j=0}^{19}C_{2^j}^{2^{19‑j}}.  

vₚ(N)=∑_{j=0}^{19}2^{19‑j}[vₚ((2^{j+1})!)-2vₚ((2^j)!)-vₚ(2^j+1)].  

Compute v₂=524 287, v₅=121 818 ⇒ k=min=121 818.  

Answer: k mod 10⁵ = 21 818.  

Pitfall: assuming any permutation possible (gives (2²⁰)!), but constraints force Catalan counts.
